reasons: Classification is sound: the Agreement contains no ownership/assignment provision — § 14(b) is limited to names/marks, § 6(a) only allocates liability for Content, and § 9(b)(viii) is a title warranty by Kubient rather than an ownership allocation — so neither the preferred nor the fallback position is met and a 'missing' finding with an inserted clause is the correct treatment.

The inserted clause reaches the preferred position with a single, self-contained addition: Customer retains all rights in Content, Properties, Requests and Customer Data (including visitor data collected by Kubient), Kubient retains its Auction Platform and pre-existing tools/know-how, deliverables are assigned with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence-back to embedded Kubient IP, and joint ownership is expressly excluded.

Direction is correct for our side (we represent the Customer/AP): no Customer IP or data is assigned to the vendor, and the vendor's platform ownership is preserved, so the edit is not over-reaching against a term that already benefits us.

Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, explains the insertion, cites the playbook position and offers the licence-in-lieu-of-assignment fallback; deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and no Customer-to-Vendor assignment remains.

Minor, non-blocking: the new text is lettered '(b)' immediately after § 6(a); if that section already contains a subsection (b), the numbering should be adjusted or the clause placed as a standalone IP section.
